items.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: I’m like Gerry Ford, I can’t eat and listen at the same time.

ctx.x: That’s a great thought. How can you – the anticipation of the music is kind of killed then, because when you come into it it’s already there.

It’s one of my real pet peeves. I mean you should come in to a room and be anticipating the music and hungry for it, just like you are for a meal. But it’s almost unheard of that a club doesn’t have the music on, right up to the moment — I mean I can’t even sometimes find time to tune up, because the music is going on right to the time the guys get on the bandstand, and there’s music playing, and I’m trying to get in tune with the piano, and the music is playing at the same time. And you know — I want silence…

It’s interesting, even tonight it looks like they have a set-up where the people are going to be eating dinner during the first significant portion of this party. These jazz parties are an interesting kind of phenomenon. Do you enjoy making the circuit on these things?
